prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
The API now requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>` with roles `viewer`, `cook` and `manager`, and writes an audit log readable at `GET /audit` (managers only). `npm test` (26 pass) and `npm run lint` pass, and a manual run confirmed the 401/403 cases and the audit listing.

Things that behave in ways you might not assume:
- **Seed keys:** `seed-viewer-key`, `seed-cook-key` and `seed-manager-key` are example keys in `data/seed.json`. I put the same ones in `data/db.json` (it was identical to the seed), otherwise `npm start` would refuse every request.
- **Schema 3:** adding `apiKeys` and `audit` bumps the schema. Upgrading an older file gives it an empty key list, so every request is refused until keys are added to the file by hand. That includes the cron call to `POST /jobs/nightly`, which now needs a manager key.
- **Cook permissions:** a cook can cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. Starting and finishing a stock-take stay manager-only.
- **What is audited:** every non-GET request from a known key gets an entry, including refused (403) and failed ones. Requests without a valid key (401) are not audited, since there is no key name and anonymous callers could otherwise grow the data file.
- **Error codes:** `unauthorized` (401) and `forbidden` (403), with English and Korean messages. The key is checked before routing, so an unknown route without a key is 401, not 404.
- **Tests:** `tests/helpers.js` sends the manager key by default and exports `auth(role)`. I also changed `tests/cli.test.js` to expect "schema 1 → 3" because of the bump. I added no new tests for auth or audit, since the task only asked to update existing ones.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
